newsitem.title: FRANCE: BoF council members to be picked early January.
newsitem.headline: BoF council members to be picked early January.

text.p: The French cabinet will select two members of the Bank of France's monetary policy council in early January because the outgoing council has not yet given its opinion on the nominees, government sources said on Tuesday.

The mandates of journalist Jean Boissonnat and banker Bruno de Maulde expire on January 6. The cabinet holds its last session of the year on Wednesday and the matter is not on the agenda, the sources said.
The next cabinet session is scheduled for January 3. "It will probably be at the very beginning of the year," a government source said.
"We are reaching the end of the procedure, but the Bank of France has to give its opinion (on the six candidates) and to our knowledge, we have not yet received it," the source said.
A member of the monetary policy council confirmed to reporters that the body had not yet discussed the issue.

Sources familiar with the process said earlier that National Assembly president Philippe Seguin, Senate president Rene Monory and Economic and Social Council (CES) head Jean Matteoli failed to agree on a list of nominees and would submit separate lists.

The sources said the main disagreement was between Monory, an ardent pro-European, and Seguin, who campaigned against the Maastricht treaty in a 1992 referendum before converting and favours a weaker franc and faster interest rate cuts.
The possible replacement of the two has unnerved financial markets, on fears the government might use it as an excuse to try and soften the Bank's policy on interest rates.
